description: Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow: profile Python, Node or Ruby apps, port the hot functions with your coding agent, prove they behave the same.

latest_release.name: v0.8.8
latest_release.body:
- `bench`: rounds with an A/A control (the original against itself), a faster/slower/noise verdict, and CPU time next to wall time (#138).
- `verify`: floats compare relative to their size (or their array's largest value), and -0.0 isn't 0.0 (#139).
- `port`: every 5th recorded call is held out from the agent, so a port can't special-case the calls it was shown (#141).
- C: the app calls the port through a typed entry point instead of JSON: no per-call JSON overhead, and NaN/infinity results come back as they are (#140).
- Python: ports build without LTO like the other languages, 4–9× faster rebuilds (#137).
- Go, C#, PHP: NaN and infinity pass between the app and the port (#130, #132, #134). Python: `Pool` workers' profiles and recordings are no longer lost (#128).
- `bench` refuses to run with no ports enabled; the report says "slower" when the app got slower; `doctor` exits 0 when scanning works without Rust (#142).

Thanks @Butterski, @mohitmishra786 and @JuggyBob.

detail.readme:
Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow.

Rewriting a whole app in Rust costs months, minute-long compiles and gigabytes of `target/`. Most of the runtime sits in a few functions anyway. **fast-anything** finds those functions, has your coding agent port *only them* to Rust, proves the port gives the same results on real recorded calls, and swaps it in. One command, fully reversible.

## Install ```sh npm i -g @el4cteo/fast-anything # or: cargo install fast-anything ``` Ports are compiled with your Rust toolchain ([rustup](https://rustup.rs)). ## Use ```sh fast-anything go --agent claude -- python app.py # or: -- node app.ts / bun app.ts / deno run -A app.ts / ruby app.rb / java App.java / mvn exec:java / gradle run / go run . / php app.php / clang -O2 main.c / Rscript app.R ``` Or step by step: | command | what it does | |---|---| | `scan -- ` | profiles the app, ranks functions by time × how portable they are | | `port [id]` | records up to 500 real calls, creates a one-function Rust crate + `TASK.md` | | `verify` | release-builds the port and replays every recorded call | | `enable` / `disable` | swaps the Rust in or out (one marked block, removed byte for byte) | | `bench` | times the whole app in rotated rounds of original, original again (an A/A control for noise) and Rust; wall and CPU time | | `report` | markdown + SVG card for your PR | | `doctor` | checks Rust, your runtimes and your agents | `--agent` takes `claude`, `codex`, or any command that reads a prompt on stdin. Without it, hand `TASK.md` to whatever you use. ## Proof, not vibes

That port looked right but compared bytes instead of characters. 148 of 500 real calls caught it. On top of the recorded calls, fast-anything derives extra cases and lets the original answer them: edge cases (NaN, ±infinity, -0.0, zero and ±1, non-ASCII text, empty and up to 16× bigger inputs) and shrunk inputs (tiny and random slices). Nothing is enabled until every case matches: same values (floats within 1e-9 of their size or of the largest value in the same list, -0.0 not 0.0), errors where the original errors. A port that is right but slower per call than the original (calling into Rust costs more than the work saved) isn't enabled either. `FAST_ANYTHING_DISABLE=1` runs the original any time. Every 5th recorded call (from 5 calls up) is held out of the crate folder the agent works in: verify replays it too but reports a mismatch there without the values, so a port that special-cases the calls it was shown still fails. ## Results Real runs on an i5-10500, Windows 11 (C and C++: a 4-core GitHub Actions Linux runner). Reproduce them from [`examples/`](examples). | app | before | after | |---|---|---| | Python fuzzy dedupe (700 names) | 4.91s | **42ms, 116×** | | TypeScript fuzzy dedupe (2,000 names) | 3.11s | **155ms, 20×** | | PHP fuzzy dedupe (600 names) | 2.94s | **53ms, 55×** | | Go fuzzy dedupe (3,000 names) | 3.02s | **144ms, 21×** | | Ruby fuzzy dedupe (400 names) | 3.13s | **228ms, 14×** | | C# fuzzy dedupe (4,000 names) | 4.03s | **312ms, 13×** | | Java fuzzy dedupe (4,000 names) | 3.50s | **1.18s, 3×** (11× on the function; the rest is JVM startup) | | C mandelbrot (8 zoom levels) | 431ms | **127ms, 3.4×** | | C++ fuzzy dedupe (6,000 names) | 3.02s | **1.09s, 2.7×** | fast-anything ports the outermost loop it can, not the tiny function called inside it, so the app crosses into Rust once instead of millions of times. Porting only the inner `levenshtein` gave 35× and 1.9×. ## Why not rewrite it all? - **Compile time**: each port is a one-function crate. Seconds, not minutes. - **Cache**: every port shares one `.fast/target`. Delete it whenever you like (`fast-anything clean`). - **Risk**: your code stays as it is. Rust is opt-in per function, checked against real behavior. ## Agents **Plugin**: the repo is an agent plugin marketplace ([`.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`](.agents/plugins/marketplace.json)) that bundles the skill and the MCP server. Install the CLI first, then: - **Codex**: `codex plugin marketplace add EL4CTEO/fast-anything`, then install `fast-anything` from `/plugins` - **Claude Code**: `/plugin marketplace add EL4CTEO/fast-anything`, then `/plugin install fast-anything@fast-anything` and `/fast-anything:fast python app.py` Or wire it up by hand: - **MCP server** (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor…), built into the binary: `claude mcp add fast-anything -- fast-anything mcp`. 8 tools: `fast_scan`, `fast_port`, `fast_verify`, `fast_enable`, `fast_disable`, `fast_bench`, `fast_report`, `fast_status`. - **Skill**: [`skills/fast-anything`](skills/fast-anything/SKILL.md) teaches any agent the loop. ## Languages | language | binding | status | |---|---|---| | Python 3.10+ | PyO3; servers and GUIs: `scan --duration 30` (stops them like Ctrl+C) | ✅ | | JavaScript / TypeScript (Node 22+, Bun, Deno 2+: `bun app.ts`, `deno run -A app.ts`) | napi-rs; servers: `scan --duration 30` (ends them with `process.exit`) | ✅ | | Ruby 3.3+ | C ABI + JSON, through Ruby's built-in Fiddle; servers: `scan --duration 30` (stops them like Ctrl+C) | ✅ | | Java 22+ (`java App.java`, Maven, Gradle) | the same C bridge, through the FFM API; servers: `scan --duration 30` | ✅ | | Kotlin/JVM (Gradle, `src/main/kotlin`, JDK 22+) | the Java bridge; top-level functions, `object` and companion members, extension functions | ✅ | | Go 1.22+ (`go run .`) | the same C bridge, through the Windows loader or dlopen (cgo); servers: `scan --duration 30` | ✅ | | PHP 8.1+ (`php app.php`) | the same C bridge, through PHP's FFI extension (`extension=ffi`); servers: `scan --duration 30` (with `pcntl`) | ✅ | | C and C++ (gcc, clang or Intel oneAPI icx/icpx: `clang -O2 main.c lib.c`) | the same C bridge (C passes its arguments as they are, no JSON), through LoadLibrary or dlopen; servers: `scan --duration 30` | ✅ | | C# / .NET 8+ (`dotnet run -c Release`) | the same C bridge, through NativeLibrary; profiled with EventPipe, nothing to install; GUIs and servers: `scan --duration 30` | ✅ | | R 4.0+ (`Rscript app.R`) | the same C bridge, through base R's `.C()`; profiled with Rprof, no packages or R headers needed; servers: `scan --duration 30` | ✅ | It ports top-level, deterministic functions that take plain data (numbers, strings, lists, dicts, typed arrays…), including ones in your entry script when its main code sits under `if __name__ == "__main__":` (or `if __FILE__ == $0`, or `if (import.meta.main)` / `if (require.main === module)`). In Python that means module-level functions, `@staticmethod`s and `@classmethod`s that don't use `cls` (dataclasses, NamedTuples and numeric NumPy arrays count as plain data), in Java, C# and PHP static methods (and PHP functions), in Go plain functions, in C and C++ free functions and static methods. `scan` says why anything else can't move yet. With Intel oneAPI on Windows, run fast-anything from a shell where `setvars.bat` ran (it sets up the linker). SYCL kernels run on the device and aren't ported; with `-fsycl`, only host functions are profiled and ported. Ruby, Java, Go, PHP, C, C++, C# and R need no headers, bindings or extra tools: the port is a plain Rust library with one C entry point taking and returning JSON, and fast-anything replays the recorded calls against it directly. Any language that can call C can use that bridge. A C port also has a typed entry point that takes the function's own arguments and returns its result, NaN and infinity included; the C app calls that one, and verify replays and times it. ## License MIT
